PT: EarthSound transforma nove visualizações ambientais da NASA em experiências sonoras acessíveis e interativas, usando dados verificados ou categorias visuais claramente identificadas.

EN: EarthSound turns nine NASA environmental visualizations into accessible, interactive sound experiences using verified data or clearly labeled visual categories.
summary: EarthSound is an accessible, bilingual web app inspired by NASA’s The Earth Information Jukebox challenge. It turns environmental observations into sound, allowing users to explore data visually and listen to patterns through interactive sonification. The MVP includes a 2021 global temperature-anomaly experience, an Antarctic ozone timeline spanning 1983–2018, and a library of nine NASA audiovisual resources. Using the Web Audio API, verified numerical data are mapped to sound features such as pitch and rhythm. When a source provides only visual categories, the sound is clearly labeled as a qualitative interpretation—not a measurement. The app supports Portuguese and English, keyboard navigation, spoken guidance, and text alternatives for browsers without voice recognition. EarthSound makes open Earth science more approachable, supports multimodal learning, and aims to broaden participation in understanding environmental change.
details:
Project Description

EarthSound turns environmental data into accessible audiovisual experiences. Inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge The Earth Information Jukebox, it lets people explore NASA visualizations and hear interpretations of the data. The MVP includes an exploration of 2021 global temperature anomalies, Antarctic ozone maps from 1983 to 2018, and a library of nine NASA audiovisual resources.

Where reliable numerical data are available, values are mapped to sound characteristics such as pitch and rhythm while the related visualization remains on screen. When a source provides only visual categories or states, the sound is identified as qualitative, not as a measurement. This helps prevent invented values or misinterpretations—for example, treating temperature anomalies as absolute temperatures. The experience also explains key references and limits: GISTEMP anomalies are relative to the 1951–1980 mean, and the ozone materials identify the 220 DU threshold.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Audio provides another way to perceive environmental patterns. It can make data exploration more accessible to people who are blind or have low vision, and support educators and audiences without a technical background. The project aims to bring people closer to open scientific data, encourage climate literacy, and show how environmental information can be understood through multiple senses. These are intended outcomes, not measured impact results.

Tools and Technologies

The MVP was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and CSS. It uses the Web Audio API to generate sound from data and the Web Speech API for spoken guidance and, where supported, voice commands. Sources include NASA Earth Information Center and Scientific Visualization Studio materials, NASA GISTEMP data, and resources from NASA Ozone Watch and NOAA. GitHub is used for version control.

No specialized hardware is required: the app runs in a browser on a computer or phone with audio. A microphone is optional; conventional controls and text alternatives allow people to use the app without voice commands.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Sonification is treated as a way to represent data—not as background music. The interface explains how data relate to sound and pairs audio with visual and textual information. The project also considers accessibility, keyboard navigation, screen readers, contrast, Portuguese and English support, and browser compatibility—including a text alternative when voice recognition is unavailable.

The team prioritized traceable sources, units, and scientific references, clear distinctions between measurements and qualitative interpretations, and preservation of NASA’s original visualizations.

Team: Anny Karoline, Isabella Marques, and Ana Luiza.
